derivations.method: Report is printed as 20:20/00:20Z at JFK with no '+1'. The Z value is read from the page, but its calendar day is derived: to_utc(JFK, 2026-09-16T20:20) = 2026-09-17T00:20Z, so the printed 00:20Z belongs to 17SEP, not the row date.
Report is printed as 00:25/23:25Z at LHR with no '+1'. Day derived: to_utc(LHR, 2026-09-27T00:25) = 2026-09-26T23:25Z, so the printed 23:25Z falls on the PREVIOUS calendar day, 26SEP.
Off duty printed 19:05/00:05Z at ORD with no '+1' (local date unchanged). Day derived: to_utc(ORD, 2026-09-04T19:05) = 2026-09-05T00:05Z.
Off duty printed 00:27/23:27Z+1. The '+1' applies to the local date (08SEP); to_utc(LHR, 2026-09-08T00:27) = 2026-09-07T23:27Z, so the UTC instant stays on 07SEP.

STA printed 00:50/23:50Z+1 and off duty 01:20/00:20Z+1 at LHR. Days derived separately: arrival to_utc(LHR, 2026-09-21T00:50) = 2026-09-20T23:50Z (still 20SEP) while off duty to_utc(LHR, 2026-09-21T01:20) = 2026-09-21T00:20Z (21SEP).
SIM detail. Report taken as the printed start of the training window, 08:00/07:00Z, with NO reporting offset applied, since crew are due at the venue rather than reporting for a sector.
